result.topic_en: Ramanujan gives formulas and the maximum order of $Q_4(N)$, the coefficients in the fourth power of the theta series, then expresses the generating function of $Q_6(N)$ (sums of six squares) through Lambert-type series, deducing an inequality with $\sigma_2(N)$ and a Dirichlet-series identity.
result.transcription:
$N$ is not a multiple of 4, then
(387) $Q_4(N) = N\cdot\frac{1-2^{-a_2-1}}{1-2^{-1}}\cdot\frac{1-3^{-a_3-1}}{1-3^{-1}}\cdot\frac{1-5^{-a_5-1}}{1-5^{-1}}\cdots\cdots\frac{1-p^{-a_p-1}}{1-p^{-1}}$;
and if $N$ is a multiple of 4, then
(388) $Q_4(N) = 3N\cdot\frac{2^{-a_2-1}}{1-2^{-1}}\cdot\frac{1-3^{-a_3-1}}{1-3^{-1}}\cdot\frac{1-5^{-a_5-1}}{1-5^{-1}}\cdots\cdots\frac{1-p^{-a_p-1}}{1-p^{-1}}$.
It is easy to see from (387) and (388) that, in order that $Q_4(N)$ should be of maximum order, $a_2$ must be 1. From (382) we see that the maximum order of $Q_4(N)$ is
(389) $\frac{3}{4}e^{\gamma}\left\{\log\log N + \frac{2(\sqrt{2}-1)}{\sqrt{(\log N)}} + S_1(\log N) + O\frac{1}{\sqrt{(\log N)}\log\log N}\right\}$
$= \frac{3}{4}e^{\gamma}\left\{\log\log N + O\frac{1}{\sqrt{(\log N)}}\right\}$.
It may be observed that, if $N$ is not a multiple of 4, then
$Q_4(N) = \sigma_1(N)$;
and if $N$ is a multiple of 4, then
$Q_4(N) = \frac{3\sigma_1(N)}{2^{a_2+1}-1}$.
73. Let $(1+2q+2q^4+2q^9+\cdots)^6$
$= 1 + 12\{Q_6(1)q + Q_6(2)q^2 + Q_6(3)q^3 + \cdots\}$
Then, by means of Elliptic functions, we can show that
(390) $Q_6(1)q + Q_6(2)q^2 + Q_6(3)q^3 + \cdots\cdots$
$= \frac{4}{3}\left(\frac{1^2q}{1+q^2} + \frac{2^2q^2}{1+q^4} + \frac{3^2q^3}{1+q^6} + \cdots\right)$
$- \frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{1^2q}{1-q} - \frac{3^2q^3}{1-q^3} + \frac{5^2q^5}{1-q^5} - \cdots\right)$.
But $\frac{5}{3}\{\sigma_2(1)q + \sigma_2(2)q^2 + \sigma_2(3)q^3 + \cdots\}$
$= \frac{4}{3}\left\{\frac{1^2q}{1-q} + \frac{2^2q^2}{1-q^2} + \frac{3^2q^3}{1-q^3} + \cdots\right\}$
$+ \frac{1}{3}\left\{\frac{1^2q}{1-q} + \frac{2^2q^2}{1-q^2} + \frac{3^2q^3}{1-q^3} + \cdots\right\}$.
It follows that
(391) $Q_6(N) \leq \frac{5\sigma_2(N)-2}{3}$,
for all values of $N$. It also follows from (390) that
(392) $\frac{4}{3}\zeta(s-2)\zeta_1(s) - \frac{1}{3}\zeta(s)\zeta_1(s-2) = 1^{-s}Q_6(1) + 2^{-s}Q_6(2) + 3^{-s}Q_6(3) + \cdots\cdots$

Multiplicative formula for $Q_4(N)$ when $N$ is divisible by 4

Upper bound for $Q_6(N)$ in terms of $\sigma_2(N)$
Dirichlet series for $Q_6(N)$ in terms of zeta functions
